title: Method and validation of synaptosomal preparation for isolation of synaptic membrane proteins from rat brain
author: Kamat, Kalani, et al.
materials: Equal amount of proteins were loaded for SDS-PAGE for separation, followed by transfer onto a nitrocellulose membrane. The membrane was kept in 1% BSA containing, Tris-buffer saline (TBS), pH 7.6 and then incubated overnight at 4 °C on slow shaking plate. Following the incubation, the membrane was washed with washing buffer (pH 7.6, TBS, 0.1% Tween 20) for 60 min and incubated with synapse protein known primary antibodies against (synaptophysin, SAP-97, SNAP-25, NMDA-R1, PSD-95) and β-actin (1:500 dilution, Santa Cruz Biotechnology, Inc.) for overnight at 40 °C, again washed with TBS-T buffer for 30 min (three washes each of 10 min) and then incubated with secondary antibody conjugated with horseradish peroxidase (1:1000 dilution, Santa Cruz Biotechnology, Inc.) for 2 h at room temperature. This was followed by washing with TBS-T for 30 min (three washes each of 10 min). Then after that those membranes were reacted with ECL reagents (Pierce Biotechnology, Inc.). Relative optical density of protein bands was analyzed using gel documentation system. Sample loading for synapse proteins were normalized with relative optical density of the β-actin band (Fig. 2B). Further quantitative analysis of protein band was done by image Lab version.3 software. Quantification of protein blots was represented by bar graph (Fig. 2C).

steps.title: Prepare sucrose gradient solutions
steps.instruction: Make 1.3 M sucrose solution by dissolving 455.83 g sucrose in 1000 ml HEPES buffer; make 0.3 M sucrose solution by dissolving 109.53 g sucrose in 1000 ml HEPES buffer; obtain a 0.8 M sucrose solution by mixing the 1.3 M and 0.3 M sucrose solutions in a 1:1 volume ratio.

steps.title: Perfuse rats and collect brains
steps.instruction: Sacrifice rats under ether anesthesia, then perfuse the heart with ice‑cold normal saline up to 50 ml to drain blood.

steps.title: Wash and chill brain tissue
steps.instruction: Remove the brain quickly, wash it with normal saline, and place it on an ice‑cold glass plate.

steps.title: Prepare homogenization buffer with inhibitors
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 % (w/v) 0.32 M sucrose‑HEPES buffer and add protease inhibitor cocktail.

steps.title: Homogenize brain tissue
steps.instruction: Suspend the brain tissue in the buffer using a Polytron homogenizer, then homogenize further with a Dounce tissue grinder for 10 even up‑and‑down strokes.

steps.title: Centrifuge homogenate to remove debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 600 × g for 10 min at 4–8 °C in a 3K300 centrifuge.

steps.title: Adjust sucrose concentration to 0.8 M
steps.instruction: Dilute the supernatant 1:1 with the 1.3 M HEPES‑sucrose solution to obtain a final sucrose concentration of 0.8 M.

steps.title: Wash synaptosomal pellet multiple times
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the suspension at 12 000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C, discard the supernatant, and repeat this wash 2–3 times to remove residual sucrose‑HEPES buffer.

steps.title: Lyse synaptosomes with RIPA + Triton
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in RIPA buffer containing protease inhibitor, PMSF, and 0.2 % Triton X‑100, then centrifuge at 20 000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend final pellet in RIPA buffer
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and resuspend the resulting pellet in RIPA buffer containing protease inhibitor and PMSF only.

steps.title: Proceed to protein quantification
steps.instruction: Use the synaptosomal preparation immediately for protein estimation and downstream biochemical assays.

steps.title: Load proteins onto SDS-PAGE gel
steps.instruction: Load equal amounts of protein samples onto an SDS‑PAGE gel for electrophoretic separation.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to nitrocellulose membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer the separated proteins from the gel onto a nitrocellulose membrane.

steps.title: Block membrane with 1% BSA
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane in 1 % BSA dissolved in Tris‑buffered saline (TBS, pH 7.6) overnight at 4 °C on a slow‑shaking platform.

steps.title: Wash membrane with TBS‑T (60 min)
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with TBS containing 0.1 % Tween‑20 (TBS‑T) for a total of 60 min.

steps.title: Incubate membrane with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with primary antibodies against synaptophysin, SAP‑97, SNAP‑25, NMDA‑R1, PSD‑95 and β‑actin (1 : 500 dilution, Santa Cruz Biotechnology) overnight at 40 °C.

steps.title: Wash membrane post‑primary incubation
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with TBS‑T three times, 10 min each (total 30 min).

steps.title: Incubate membrane with HRP secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate with HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody (1 : 1000 dilution, Santa Cruz Biotechnology) for 2 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash membrane post‑secondary incubation
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with TBS‑T three times, 10 min each (total 30 min).

steps.title: Develop blot with ECL reagents
steps.instruction: React the membrane with ECL detection reagents (Pierce Biotechnology) to visualize protein bands.

steps.title: Image and quantify protein bands
steps.instruction: Capture images using a gel documentation system, analyze relative optical density of bands, normalize synaptic protein signals to β‑actin, and quantify using Image Lab version 3 software.
